title: camera rig: two rooms
shortDescription: Two rooms of an abandoned observatory in a .glb from Blender, seen through its cameras: a click walks the camera to the other room, a drag looks around, the wheel flies through the door along a camera animated in Blender, and a lift clears the picture for the observing log
description:
A `.glb` made in Blender: the control room of an abandoned observatory — green terminals, a desk lamp, moonlight through the blinds — and the dome behind its steel door, a refractor under the open slit, a red safelight. Its light is baked into one texture, so the scene needs no light of its own. The asset brings three cameras: one in each room and one animated through the door, the clip *through_the_door*.

`new Stage2D(new CameraProjection(camera))` looks through the camera of the control room, fitted as Blender framed it: a narrow screen shows all of the frame, with more above and below ([Looking through a camera](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#looking-through-a-camera-cameraprojection)). A `CameraRig` moves it. **A click** is `rig.moveTo(camera, 1.8)`: the camera of the stage walks over to the camera of the other room — position, orientation and field of view — and locks on to it ([A camera animated in Blender](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#a-camera-animated-in-blender)). **A drag** is `rig.look({yaw, pitch})`, on top of whatever the camera shows, until the next target. **The wheel** — or the slider — runs a track: `rig.track([{at: 0, shot: controlRoom}, {at: 0.12, until: 0.88, shot: flyCamera, clip: flight}, {at: 1, shot: dome}])`, and `rig.lerp(t, {smooth: 0.25})` glides along it; inside the middle key the progress scrubs the clip of the animated camera, forward and back ([A page that scrolls through a scene](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#a-page-that-scrolls-through-a-scene)). **L** opens the observing log over the lower part of the screen, and `rig.reframe({lift: 0.3}, 0.5)` moves the picture up through the view offset of the camera, without turning it ([Lifting the picture over a dialog](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#lifting-the-picture-over-a-dialog)); the lift holds through every move.
